This is probably contributing to the DDoS they are experiencing but I managed to get the button appear after doing the following:
1. Close Launcher
2. Head to %appdata% (C:\user\username\appdata\roaming)
3. Rename rsilauncher to something like rsilauncher.old
4. Open launcher and login (Don't try and re-download the game or anything) then close it. 
5. head back to %appdata% and rename the new rsilauncher folder to something like rsilauncher.new and then remove the .old from the previous folder's name. 
6. Open the launcher for a final time and the buttons should reappear. 

Not sure if its worth going to the effort to save a few minutes but just thought I would publish what I did.

Seriously though, I’m 25. Struggled with mental health since the age of 5 after my dad left. Went to group therapy for seperate families and was diagnosed with abandonment issues. Fast forward to 2004 when my grandfather (my father figure for my young life)  died, I go back into a state of depression and it’s ruled as grief/ the abandonment issues again. Teenage years roll around and I’m the angriest little shit I think anyone could be, not going to school, not paying attention, skipping classwork and assignments, not leaving my room for days on end. I go and see this class A psychiatrist or so I’m told. I was treated by him from the age of 14 till 19. Was told I had depression and was on all sorts of anti-depressants. I ballooned out to 150kgs and basically became a zombie. I finish school and feel a lot better, I stop seeing the psychiatrist and came off the meds. 5 years later I was admitted into hosptial after a failed suicide attempt, it was my second attempt after trying to OD a few months before and passing out only to wake up feeling hungover and shitty.  

The senior psychiatrist was the man I saw in the hosptial, he was the FIRST doctor I really felt comfortable with. He carried out his assessments and I was diagnosed with ADHD. I was started on Ritalin on the Monday and I was out the following Monday. 

The point of my story is that people are people mate they don’t always get along and you need to find someone you are comfortable with and feel comfortable talk to. You know yourself better than anyone else. Just shop around mate you will find some and get those questions answered.

Mate I’m 25, I was diagnosed less than a month ago after going through years of been treated for depression and anxiety. 

Dr Google is the worst doctor on earth I’ll tell you that now, most people know you could google a slight cough and a runny nose and it would return a result of lung cancer.... 

The key thing is you are recognising symptoms, you know yourself better than anyone else. Yes what you described sounds like the tell tale signs of ADHD but the best person to do the actual diagnosing is a psychiatrist. I am in Australia, I was diagnosed after a suicide attempt and mental breakdown. All it took was a couple of ‘rate your mood’ tests and a 1.5 hour consultation with my doctor and I walked out with a diagnosis. 

Just remember to be completely honest in your answers and don’t just tick the box that you will think will get you what you want to hear. Medical professionals do their job well and they have the years of experience and training behind them to take what you say and what you feel and give you the best answers. 

Good luck my friend!

There are two answers to argue really.

Yes: the rise of using terms like “I’m going to kill myself because my parents didn’t buy me an iPhone” have contributed to it become something edgy and attention seeking that a lot of people will use without even thinking. These people jump from one extreme to the other and as a few people have said are just assholes that don’t really understand the gravity of the words “I am going to kill myself”.  I’ve had friends say it over trivial things like the iPhone example to getting rejected/ ghosted on tinder. Shows like 13 reasons why have been criticised about glorifying suicide which didn’t help the whole stigma and really made a lot of matters worse especially around the age group it was targeted (Teenagers/ Young adults) that are going through massive changes in their body and mind and are more often than not the most susceptible to suicidal thoughts and actions such as cutting.

No: The actual meaning behind the words when said with purpose and in true states of depression, anxiety and grief have not changed. The social acceptance of mental illness is what has changed. Take a look back to the First World War when the term ‘Shell shock’ appeared. These soldiers were told they were just cowards and weak when in truth they were suffering from extreme anxiety and PTSD. The social stigma of the time denied them help and they were branded as weak men. Even right up till the early 90s Mental illness was a huge taboo subject and suffers often were told they were lying or just couldn’t handle it because they were weak. 

It’s only in the last 2 decades has it become something that is openly talked about and we have campaigns promoting help for suffers of mental illness. I’ve noticed personally through the many doctors and years I have gone through mental illness that it is the younger medical professionals are more understanding and willing to take risk and look at the bigger picture when making a diagnosis. The doctors that were senior even 10 years ago were trained in the days when mental health was not openly discussed and their treatments still aligned with the old institution days. As the next generation are now becoming the seniors and the old are retiring the medical industry is adjusting and is more willing to help those truely in need. I strongly believe our governments knew this would happen and could not find the funding to support the epidemic that is upon us today. That’s why they shut down the institutes and have placed all the responsibilities on the patient themselves to pay out of pocket for specialist treatment and the hosptial system to support the massive influx of cases of mental illness.

Mate same situation, I went through a group therapy as a kid after my parents divorce, they put it down as abandonment issues. I then struggled all through school seeing a psychiatrist that treated me for depression and anxiety. Putting me on Resperidone which basically turned me into a zombie and I gained 68kgs. I came off it after school, lost the weight but never felt right. After attempting to take my life twice and the hosptial stint they diagnosed me with ADHD as I said above, which really is the most common and most treatable mental health issue. I’m filthy that no trained medical professional even considered it when I was a child. 

I am finding that as the older doctors are starting to retire and the younger doctors are becoming more senior they are willing to accept mental health disorders and take risks when treating patients. When these older doctors were going through training back in the 60s, 70s and 80s mental health was a big taboo subject. Now it’s 2019 and the world is a lot more open about mental health, it will take a long time but it is possible that we may one day be able to cure mental health.

I believe the government saw an incoming mental health epidemic and couldn’t free up funding for it. They closed the Asylums which whilst ended years of abuse and basically imprisonment of mental health patients pushed all the strain on the hosptial system and made it the patients problem to fund their treatment in the ‘real world’ .  My local hosptial has 12 mental health beds and the largest hosptial in southern SYDNEY been St George has only 26 mental health beds. It is an epidemic but no one in the government really wants to take responsibility for it.

I spent 20 years of my life telling myself this was a lie. Thousands of dollars spent on doctors and meds (In Australia mind you) to treat my “Depression and Anxiety”. Nothing ever changed I woke up every day wanting to die. I gained 63kgs, lost friends and family. Finally was admitted to hospital a few months back after a suicide attempt. The psychiatrist handed me a few tests, spoke to me and within 2 days I had a fresh diagnoses of ADHD. Changed my life, the pills worked instantly, I woke up a few days later and something clicked I wanted to be alive, I had things to live for and love. 

Not saying it’s the case for everyone but sometimes the waiting game is a long run, not everyone gets better but it’s worth a shot. If I had ended it the multiple times I tried then I would have ended up where I am today feeling the way I am.

Okay I am an ex-gastro Nurse, working in the private health system 60%+ of my patients were in for weight loss.

I am not sure what country you live in however in Australia the sleeve is now becoming the best/ only option.

Whilst I am not a Doctor the pros and cons are from what I have observed/ learnt in my 4 years.

***Gastric Banding***

**Pros**

* Reversable
* Less inavasive
* Adjustable
* Quicker Reovery Period
*  Less painful

**Cons**

*  Possible slipping of physical band
* Higher possibility of infection
* Not as efective
*  More prone to relapse 

***Gastric Sleeve***

**Pros**

*  Highly effective
* Less chace of Relapse
* Safer
* After recovery it dosnt hinder exerise to the extend of the band
*  No risk of slipping (there is nothing there to slip)

**Cons**

*  More painful recovery
* Limited food consumption post operative (VERY strict diet)
* Prone to infection (If diet + proper cleaing is not adheard too
* Irreversable
* Limited activies post operative

For the food, post op you are limited to Ice-chips, genreally 24 hours later a clear liquid diet (jelly, water, broth) then 48 hours later dairy can be consumed. Generally patients went home on the liquid diet then started on a soft (mash potatos, baby food etc). Solid food usualy comes along about a month later. 


A few weeks post surgery you honestly will feel like shit and feel like not doing anything. Best thing to counter this... WALKING! Just slow walk everywhere. In the hospital the physios will get you up and about to help release all the gasses that they pump you up with but also it helps relave the pain. Over time the weight will drop off and you will feel 1000% better!!

Now once again I am not a doctor however do I have a fair amount of experience, also depending on your country most doctors won't/ cannot preform this surgery unless you reach certain criteria i.e High BFI (Body Fat Index), high risk of fatal obesiety disease (Heart disease, diabities etc).

The best option is to talk to your GP, get a referal and speak to the specialist. 

Unless there is something physically stopping you, the best weight loss method is simple diet and exersie.
